inspiration.paper: OpenAI, Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation, 2026-10-25
inspiration.scope: The earlier review studied positive auxiliary energy and the planar appendix. This update does not use the wave theorem, a claim of complete external proof verification, or a locally compiled Lean artifact.

inherited_inputs: Exact default disk-smearing energy decomposition, radial/angular orthogonality, and old holomorphic/first-mixed angular Gram.
Author global radius/subset conditions and previous all-n elementary attainable-gap bound.
Certified n100 integer-witness gap upper, stationary k=2,3 coefficients, and the prior shifted-Gram layer/centered-hole certificates.
Unmodified exact original Gaussian-transfer review, imported with its report, source manifest and ZIP.
new_derivations: Certified rotation-filtered Gaussian disk means and complete cross Gram, retaining negative off-diagonal entries.
Exact cross terms against old holomorphic and first mixed tests, checked by an independent Gaussian-Laplacian formula.
Fixed rational interval-matrix duals: two scales improve the specified complete old k=4 projection by more than 5.9 percent at a real normalized nine-point input.
A full normalized one-parameter family retains more than five percent projection improvement; not an independent coordinate box.
All self-similar scales and rotations share one certified norm, giving a uniform smoothed angular-contrast bound.
Conditional n100 local-density contrast bounds 0.4285, 0.114 and 0.351, with exact layer/moment/centered-hole hypotheses.
review: One research agent derived and checked the update. Independent checks include original-review replay, exponentials versus atanh logarithms, Laplace integral recurrences, boundary-jump versus Gaussian-Laplacian cross terms, actual point measurements and independent product-gap reports. No independent-agent or external peer review is claimed.
acceptance: Four new and twenty prior exact standard-library entries, original imported-review replay, active exceptions under -O, pinned bytes and fresh extracted-package replay.
limitations: The smoothing/heat/Gaussian identities and Hilbert duality are standard; no invention or global priority claim is made.
The real nine-point input and its family are not asserted stationary or optimal; comparison is against the specified old k=4 tests, not all old criteria.
The all-scale statistic is a smooth Gaussian-weighted contrast, not hard disk population discrepancy or a microscopic lattice classification.
Automatic interval arithmetic has explicit parameter budgets; mathematical scale invariance is proved independently of finite-scale tests.
Higher old modes or mixed tests not included in a Gram may overlap with Gaussian probes and cannot simply be added.
No full n100 five-layer theorem, general finite-n optimal configuration, full eight-point sharp result or new unconditional M_n bound is claimed.
